guidance.heading: Full Year 2026 Guidance
section: The Company increased its target for revenue to $5.790 billion to $5.830 billion

desk.headline: Revenue up 21% to $1.36bn, just below estimates; EPS $1.33 beat; full-year guidance raised for the second time
results: Revenue rose 21% to $1.36bn and net income jumped to $277.9m from $106.8m; adjusted EBITDA rose 54% to $555.7m.
UFC led the way: revenue up 60% to $519.2m on the new Skydance media deal, two extra events and a record UFC 329.
WWE revenue slipped 1% to $399.3m on three fewer premium live events and lower SummerSlam ticket sales, but its EBITDA still rose 5%.
IMG revenue rose 16% to $391.3m and EBITDA 89% to $115.9m, helped by FIFA World Cup hospitality.
Over $1.6bn returned to holders so far this year; $936m of the buyback authority is left and TKO plans to use it, mainly with new debt.

guidance.summary: Full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA targets were raised again (first raised in August). The outlook assumes all live events, including those in the Middle East, go ahead as planned.

points: Management said lower WrestleMania and SummerSlam ticket sales were planned, not a sign of weaker demand.
The FIFA World Cup brought IMG about $90m of EBITDA for the year, ahead of a roughly $75m plan.
Guidance assumes one WWE and two UFC events in the Middle East go ahead despite regional conflict; WrestleMania 2027 is set for Saudi Arabia.
The remaining buyback will be funded mostly by new debt, so net leverage of about 2.0x is set to rise.
A March investor day was flagged, where the partnerships target could be raised.
call.source: Call coverage: Earnings Whispers (via Finviz), 4 Nov 2026

watch: How much new debt is taken on to finish the $936m buyback.
Whether Middle East events proceed as assumed in the guidance.
Growth in 2027 once the one-off World Cup boost at IMG falls away.
